bib.title: Hurdles to Progress in Long-form Question Answering

question: Do current long-form question answering systems, datasets (ELI5) and metrics (ROUGE-L, human A/B tests) support meaningful measurement of progress?
contributions: A state-of-the-art ELI5 system: Routing Transformer generator conditioned on passages from a contrastively trained REALM retriever (C-REALM)
Showing generations are not grounded in retrieved documents (random-retrieval control)
Showing at least 81% of ELI5 validation questions have a paraphrase in the training set
Showing ROUGE-L is gameable and uninformative for LFQA, via lower and upper bounds
Describing the difficulty of human evaluation for LFQA, with suggestions for each issue

method.summary: A C-REALM dense retriever (BERT-base, trained with in-batch contrastive loss against gold answers, batch 12,288) feeds top-7 Wikipedia paragraphs to a 486M Routing Transformer pretrained on PG-19 and fine-tuned on ELI5. The system tops the KILT ELI5 leaderboard, and control experiments (random retrievals, train/validation question overlap, trivial ROUGE-L baselines, human A/B tests) are used to show the evaluation is flawed.
method.task: long-form question answering (ELI5, KILT) with retrieval-augmented generation

datasets.name: ELI5 (KILT version)
datasets.split: KILT train/validation/test; test answers hidden, scored on EvalAI leaderboard
datasets.source: Fan et al. 2019, downloaded from the KILT GitHub repository
datasets.preprocessing: retrievals, questions and answers truncated/padded to 288 subword tokens (PG19 subword tokenizer); loss not computed on padding

datasets.name: PG-19
datasets.size: about 28,000 Project Gutenberg books, 1.9B tokens, average context 69K words

datasets.name: Wikipedia (KILT knowledge source)
datasets.source: paragraph-length chunks; index size 15B parameters per Table 10 (as printed)

datasets.name: CC-News (REALM pretraining)
datasets.source: REALM-CCNews checkpoint used to initialise C-REALM

datasets.name: Quora Question Paraphrase (GLUE)
datasets.source: used to fine-tune a RoBERTa-large paraphrase classifier; 37% of QQP pairs are valid paraphrases

models.name: C-REALM retriever
models.architecture: BERT-base encoder with final projection to 128-d shared embedding space; shared query/candidate encoders; MIPS with ScaNN

models.name: Routing Transformer (RT) generator
models.architecture: sparse-attention decoder (local attention plus mini-batch k-means routing attention), fine-tuned decoder-only

other.input_format: [r_K, r_K-1 ... r_1, q, a] with retrieved paragraphs reversed so top-ranked is nearest the answer; special separator symbols

training.objective: Retriever: in-batch softmax contrastive loss pushing question vector toward its gold answer vector and away from other answers in the mini-batch (distant supervision, after Jernite 2020). Generator: next-token prediction of answer tokens given retrievals and question, loss only on last 288 answer tokens.
training.batch_size: retriever 12,288 (192 per chip across 64 accelerators); generator 128 QA pairs (332k tokens per mini-batch, 37k loss tokens)
training.steps: retriever 4k steps (best at 1.5k, early stopping on validation with batch 512); generator 100k steps
training.seq_len: 288 subword tokens per retrieval/question/answer; model max 8192
training.dropout: 15% input, attention and ReLU dropout (generator), described as critical to prevent overfitting
training.hardware: 64 Google Cloud TPUs (v3 chips per A.1 note on BERT-base fitting a TPU v3 chip); retriever validation on P100 GPU
training.compute: final models trained using 64 Google Cloud TPUs for a total of 32 hours
training.wall_clock: retriever 103 minutes for 4k steps (43 minutes to best at 1.5k steps); generator about 30 hours for 100k steps (0.92 steps/second)

other.framework: TensorFlow 1.15 and Tensor2Tensor; REALM and Routing Transformer codebases
other.hyperparameter_selection: chosen manually with minimal tuning; no hyperparameter search for final generator
other.retriever_init_ablation: REALM-CCNews init beats ICT init and BERT init; Table 9 text says minibatch 12228 (typo for 12288)

inference.top_p: 0.6 and 0.9 reported; value tuned from 0.0 to 1.0 in steps of 0.1 on validation performance
inference.samples: one generation per question implied; seeds not stated
inference.prompting: decoder-only concatenation of retrievals, question and answer (no natural-language prompt)
inference.retrieval: C-REALM or REALM, MIPS with ScaNN, K = 7 paragraphs

parameters.random_retrieval_control: at inference, replace retrieved paragraphs with randomly sampled Wikipedia paragraphs

other.generation_length: 187.3 tokens on average at p=0.6 (Table 11); 187 words avg. in text; BART demo 59 words avg.

metrics.name: ROUGE-L (R-L)
metrics.definition: maximum overlap of generation with a set of gold answers (about 12 per question)

metrics.name: unigram F1
metrics.definition: maximum unigram F1 against gold answers

metrics.name: R-precision (RPr.)
metrics.definition: top-1 retrieval matches human-annotated relevant Wikipedia article (KILT)

metrics.name: KILT R-L (KRL)
metrics.definition: ROUGE-L but scored 0 whenever the top-1 retrieval does not match the gold annotation

metrics.name: n-gram overlap with retrievals
metrics.definition: fraction of generation 1-grams/2-grams (and lemmatized nouns, proper nouns, numbers not in the question) present in retrieved paragraphs

metrics.name: Human A/B preference
metrics.definition: annotators pick the better of two answers in random order, or Tie

metrics.name: Fleiss kappa
metrics.definition: agreement of 3 crowd-workers on paraphrase labels

baselines: trivial lower bounds (copy question 5 times, random training answer)
upper bounds (longest/best gold answer, best top-K train answer)
eval.protocol: Test on KILT ELI5 leaderboard (EvalAI); analysis on validation set (1,507). Paraphrase study: 300 validation questions, 7 nearest training questions retrieved by C-REALM, 3 AMT workers each (0 no paraphrase, 1 similar topic, 2 approx same question), majority label, manually verified; workers paid 4 cents per pair ($8-12/hr), USA/UK/Australia, 95% approval, 1000+ HITs. A/B tests: 20 volunteer CS graduate students, Wikipedia search allowed, three questions (answers question better, more coherent, more factual), question 1 prioritised, Tie allowed. No significance tests reported.

availability.data: generations released as supplementary HTML files; lower-bound baselines submitted to KILT leaderboard as 'Metrics Test'

results.quote: there is almost no correlation (Spearman ρ = 0.09) between the Predicted model’s generation quality and the amount of unigram overlap between its outputs and the retrieved documents

results.claim: Annotators took about 2 minutes per answer pair and were unfamiliar with technical topics, making correctness judgments hard.
results.setup: interviews with the volunteer annotators of the A/B tests
results.quote: Annotators reported taking an average of 2 minutes per answer pair

limits: A/B tests give relative preference only, not an absolute quality measure; annotators reported both answers sometimes very good and sometimes very poor (A.5).
Human raters were 20 mostly computer-science graduate student volunteers, not domain experts; no significance tests; some Table 15 cells have fewer than 50 samples.
Overlap annotation covers only 300 validation questions; the no-overlap subset has just 53 samples; Fleiss kappa only 0.29.

The grounding failure is shown for this one system (and indirectly via leaderboard comparisons for others); authors do not test other generators. Explanations (source-reference divergence, train/validation overlap, pretraining on long text) are hypotheses.
Generator hyperparameters chosen manually with no search; no seeds or variance reported.
Upper bounds are validation-only because test answers are hidden; the 'best top-K train answer' is an oracle.
Dated: 2021 models (BART, RAG, T5-base), TensorFlow 1.15; no LLM-judge or faithfulness metrics evaluated.

terms.definition: contrastive REALM: REALM-initialised BERT-base dense retriever trained with an in-batch contrastive loss against gold answers
ROUGE-L, but assigns a score of 0 whenever the top-1 retrieval does not match the gold annotation
trivial baselines used to test the vulnerability of datasets or metrics to simple heuristic strategies that do not actually perform the task

figures.caption: A summary of the major hurdles (a-d) to progress in long-form question answering with ELI5.
figures.why: Shows all four hurdles with a single example (EMP question): paraphrased training questions, random train answer ROUGE-L, random retrievals, annotator difficulty.

figures.caption: Human evaluation results with exact number of ratings shown in (·).
figures.why: Shows no preference between predicted and random retrievals and strong preference for gold answers.

figures.caption: Upper (↑) and lower (↓) bounds to performance on ELI5.
figures.why: Shows trivial baselines near real systems and upper bounds only slightly higher, which is the ROUGE-L argument.
